classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the second percentage uses the changed amount as its base, choose a convenient original100, compute that changed quantity and divide the restoring difference by it. This is a routine linked reverse-percentage application of the explicitly taught change-rate and multiplier methods, with preceding restoration examples; repeated eight numerical cases and rounding add no unsignposted model or proof.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find, correct to 2 decimal places, the percentage decrease necessary to restore a quantity to its original value if it has been increased by:

answer.worked:
Take the original quantity as $100$. The increased quantity is $110$, so the restoring decrease is $10$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage decrease}&=\frac{10}{110}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&\approx9.09\%\end{align*}$$

Take the original quantity as $100$. The increased quantity is $122$, so the restoring decrease is $22$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage decrease}&=\frac{22}{122}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&\approx18.03\%\end{align*}$$

Take the original quantity as $100$. The increased quantity is $340$, so the restoring decrease is $240$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage decrease}&=\frac{240}{340}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&\approx70.59\%\end{align*}$$

Take the original quantity as $100$. The increased quantity is $102.3$, so the restoring decrease is $2.3$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage decrease}&=\frac{2.3}{102.3}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage decrease}&\approx2.25\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find, correct to 2 decimal places, the percentage increase necessary to restore a quantity to its original value if it has been decreased by:

answer.worked:
Take the original quantity as $100$. The decreased quantity is $90$, so the restoring increase is $10$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage increase}&=\frac{10}{90}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&\approx11.11\%\end{align*}$$

Take the original quantity as $100$. The decreased quantity is $78$, so the restoring increase is $22$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage increase}&=\frac{22}{78}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&\approx28.21\%\end{align*}$$

Take the original quantity as $100$. The decreased quantity is $25$, so the restoring increase is $75$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage increase}&=\frac{75}{25}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&=300.00\%\end{align*}$$

Take the original quantity as $100$. The decreased quantity is $97.7$, so the restoring increase is $2.3$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage increase}&=\frac{2.3}{97.7}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&\approx2.35\%\end{align*}$$
